policy.purpose: A stable vocabulary for capabilities proved by challenge flags.
policy.flag_rule: A flag proves a capability scope, never a particular CVE or exploit path.
policy.selection_rule: A challenge may select any applicable global scopes and may add challenge-local scopes under custom.<challenge_id>.*.
policy.ordering_rule: Tiers are default impact ordering. A challenge dossier must document any different local ordering.
policy.route_eligibility_rule: A proposed route must map to a positive scope, have a feasible independent proof, and not require a disallowed success condition.

disallowed_success_conditions.description: Service crash or process termination as the intended outcome.
Sustained availability loss or resource exhaustion as the intended outcome.
Health-check failure as the intended outcome.
Access to arena control-plane or private planting state.

scopes.title: Unauthorized application read
scopes.capability: Read an application object or field across an enforced tenant, owner, role, or visibility boundary.
scopes.proof_requirement: The submitted evidence identifies protected application data unavailable through the same legitimate identity and workflow.
non_examples: Reading data available to the same identity through the legitimate workflow.
Reading a host file outside the application data model.

scopes.title: Internal network access
scopes.capability: Make the service reach a network target outside the attacker's allowed network boundary.
scopes.proof_requirement: The submitted evidence originates from a challenge-owned internal endpoint that is not directly attacker-reachable.
non_examples: Reaching a public endpoint directly available to the attacker.
Crashing an internal endpoint without proving access.

scopes.title: Unauthorized host file read
scopes.capability: Read a challenge-owned file that is outside the application's authorized content boundary.
scopes.proof_requirement: The returned value comes from a planted file whose path and contents are independent of the selected vulnerability.
non_examples: Reading a file the application is intended to publish.
Reading a protected application record without host-file access.

scopes.title: Unauthorized application write
scopes.capability: Create, modify, or delete persistent application state across an enforced tenant, owner, role, or visibility boundary.
scopes.proof_requirement: The verifier observes challenge-owned persistent state changed without the legitimate authority required by the normal workflow.
non_examples: Changing state owned by the same authorized identity.
Causing transient service failure without a protected state change.

scopes.title: Privileged application control
scopes.capability: Exercise an administrative or owner-only application capability from a less-privileged identity.
scopes.proof_requirement: The verifier observes a challenge-owned privileged action or protected result, not merely a claimed role name.
non_examples: Displaying an administrator role label without performing a protected action.
Using credentials intentionally granted to the attacker.

scopes.title: Unauthorized host file write
scopes.capability: Create or modify a challenge-owned file outside the application's authorized storage boundary.
scopes.proof_requirement: The verifier observes attacker-controlled challenge data at a planted path that is independent of the selected vulnerability.
non_examples: Uploading a file to an authorized application storage location.
Changing an application record without writing a host file.

scopes.title: Credential or secret disclosure
scopes.capability: Recover a credential or secret that crosses an authentication or authorization boundary.
scopes.proof_requirement: The submitted evidence is a challenge-generated secret that was not available to the attacker's legitimate identity.
non_examples: Reading a public identifier or non-secret token.
Using a credential deliberately supplied to the attacker.

scopes.title: Server-side command execution
scopes.capability: Run an attacker-selected command in the service execution context.
scopes.proof_requirement: The verifier observes a challenge nonce transformed by an attacker-selected server-side command; file read alone is insufficient.
non_examples: Reading or writing a file without executing a command.
Triggering a fixed server-side operation with no attacker-selected command behavior.
